$comment: Hand-written stand-in for `prism --help --json`. Replaced, not edited, once the CLI emits its own description. Verbs and flags follow the agreed v1.0 verb list.

globalFlags.meaning: Print the result as one JSON object instead of text.
Enable one experimental feature by name for this invocation.
Print usage for the verb and exit 0.

exitCodes.name: pass
exitCodes.meaning: The verb did what you asked and every check it ran passed.

exitCodes.name: fail
exitCodes.meaning: A check failed, an intent sentence is unproved, or a replay diverged.

exitCodes.name: cannot verify
exitCodes.meaning: No verdict was reached: a missing attestation, an unreachable registry or an unknown format revision.

prismCode.$comment: What ships today: the prism-code command as published on npm. A test compares these verbs with the command's own --help, so the list cannot drift from the binary.
prismCode.needs: Node.js 22 or later, and nothing else. Every command runs in this process; LexLean and Lean's kernel ship in the package as WebAssembly, so no command needs a network, a server or a container. `--help` after any command prints that command's usage and runs nothing.

exitCodes.name: ok
exitCodes.meaning: The verb did what you asked, or `check` reached a verdict the policy accepts.

exitCodes.name: vectors failed
exitCodes.meaning: A theorem of the model is not proved, at least one acceptance vector did not replay or the holo carries none, `replay` diverged, `verify-attestation` did not verify, `check` reached a verdict the policy rejects, or `pull` found a digest that does not match or a holo that fails verification and wrote nothing.

exitCodes.name: refused
exitCodes.meaning: The holo, capability file or manifest cannot be read or fails its checks, the model does not check, an identity check failed, a guest import, the holo's world or a provider is not granted, or a provider failed; or `check` reached no verdict: not a holo, an unreadable policy or an unknown format revision; or `push` or `pull` got no answer: an unreachable registry, refused credentials, a reference that does not exist or referrers that cannot be stored; or an export's bytes differ from the build manifest; or `generate` refused to write: the guest does not conform to its world, or a file in the output directory is not one it wrote; or `replay` could not be carried out.

exitCodes.name: signing failed
exitCodes.meaning: `attest` could not sign, or the optional sigstore packages are not installed.

exitCodes.name: proof mismatch
exitCodes.meaning: `run` refused a holo for a proof reason. 11 is a world mismatch, 12 a determinism violation, 13 a replay error.

exitCodes.name: untyped
exitCodes.meaning: Dispatch threw something untyped: a guest trap, or a bug in the runtime.

verbs.name: run
verbs.summary: With a project folder, or nothing inside one: build it when the model changed since its last build, which checks the model, proves every theorem and replays every acceptance vector in this process, then run exactly the holo that build wrote, pinned by its digest; no signature is needed for what was proved here. With a holo: check it against the policy; with no `--policy`, a holo the default policy refuses that carries its proof record is proved again in this process, its vectors replayed, and then run, pinned by its digest, so whoever runs a holo re-checks it and no signature is needed. A holo that carries no proof record is judged by the default policy. With an input, this is one run as a container: dispatch the input, print the output and exit with the container's code, keeping the container until `rm` unless `--rm`. Without one, serve its view on a local port; a POST to `/_hologram/intent` dispatches one request. A holo that fails check is refused unless `--allow-unverified`, which warns on every start.

verbs.name: rm
verbs.summary: Remove containers, by id or unique id prefix. A running container is refused.

verbs.name: init
verbs.summary: Start a Prism application. `npx prism-code@latest init` is the one command every app begins with: it writes the canonical template, `UOR-Foundation/template` (contract 2, the standalone frame), with its LexLean app in `app/`, its ledgers in `model/` and its scenarios in `features/suites/`, then `prism.toml` naming the app, `prism.project` holding an ID made once from 32 random bytes, which names the project's holospace and which no build reads, and the Prism skill for an agent, all inside the folder, and prints the steps that follow. There is no choice of template: every app, simple or complex, starts from the same one. The package carries it, and each file is admitted by its BLAKE3 label before any is written. A folder that already holds a model keeps it and gets only the skill, so the command is safe to run again; `--no-skill` leaves the skill out. Nothing outside the folder is written or configured, and nothing is fetched. `npm create prism-code` runs the same command.

verbs.name: manifest
verbs.summary: Check and lint the project's `prism.toml`, with the overlay for the target merged in, and print the application, the grant and the variables.

verbs.name: providers
verbs.summary: `up` runs the `prism-provider-<type>` each capability in `prism.toml` declares and prints the variables it produced, and `down` releases them. Text output names them, and `--json` also prints their values. The capability set must allow the type and each variable. Experimental.

verbs.name: vectors
verbs.summary: Replay every acceptance vector the holo carries, each on a fresh instance, and exit 1 on a failure. An altered holo is refused; `--allow-unverified` replays it and still exits 1. `--json` prints one `prism/report/1` report with a row for each vector: whether it passed, and the bytes of its request and response.

verbs.name: record
verbs.summary: Write the acceptance vectors the image carries as a recording, its first. `history` is the deprecated spelling, kept through 0.8.

verbs.name: replay
verbs.summary: Re-execute recordings, or every recording in a directory, against this build and compare every outcome: exit 0 unchanged, 1 diverged, 2 could not replay. `--statement` writes the `prism/replay/v1` statement, also on a divergence.

verbs.name: inspect
verbs.summary: Print what the holo says about itself, without running it, or a container's state, exit code, image digest and output.

verbs.name: attest
verbs.summary: Sign an in-toto statement about the holo into its attestation section: keyless with an OIDC token, or with `--key`. `--unsigned` signs the statements the build left unsigned, and `--statement <file>` signs a whole statement, such as the proof statement in the verified directory.

verbs.name: verify-attestation
verbs.summary: Check the holo's attestations against the signer you expect, or against `--key`.

verbs.name: export
verbs.summary: Write a release's six-file browser export or tarball, byte-checked against the build manifest, attestations beside.

verbs.name: generate
verbs.summary: Write bindings and a typed client (`--lang` js, the default, rust or python) from the holo's WIT world and model into `<dir>`, with a record of what they came from. A second run with the same inputs writes nothing.

verbs.name: publish-model
verbs.summary: Write the LexLean model in `--project` into `<dir>/model`, with `<dir>/app.holo.json` naming the holo and the model identity the holo gives, so the model can be opened and held to the app in a browser. Writes nothing when the holo names no model identity or the folder is no LexLean project.

verbs.name: lock
verbs.summary: Write the project's `lexlean.lock` again after `lexlean.toml`, a workspace file or a lexicon of the project's own changed: the project renamed or re-bounded, a lexicon edited or added in a folder. The lock is proposed from the project's files and judged by LexLean as WebAssembly, which checks it byte for byte, so nothing is written unless LexLean accepts it as the lock it would have written. `--check` writes nothing and exits 1 when the lock is not current. A project that newly needs a package embedded in LexLean which the lock does not hold, a Git package, a source package or a PDF provider is refused with exit 2. `--json` prints one `prism/report/1` report.

verbs.name: check
verbs.summary: With a project, or nothing: check its model and prove every theorem, in this process, and write nothing. It reads `prism.toml`; in a workspace that keeps the template's ledgers (`model/ids.toml`) it runs the template contract's ratchet over them and the scenarios, reporting each violation with a `contract.` code (under `template/2` ledgers, each build ID's named theorems must be proved, each refusal `model/ids.toml` lists must answer an acceptance vector, and the universal policy must have the BLAKE3 labels `template.lock` binds; `build` writes `CONFORMANCE.md` from `model/ids.toml`, and `check` only compares); then LexLean as WebAssembly checks the model, then Lean's own kernel, as WebAssembly, proves each theorem within its declared axioms. `--json` prints one `prism/report/1` report: `ok`, a `summary` and `diagnostics`, each with a code, a file, a line, a message and often a remediation. Exit 0 when it passed, 1 when a theorem is not proved or the contract is violated, 2 when the manifest or the model does not check. With a holo: judge the holo against a policy and print its verdict, the assurance level, whether the policy passed, and every reason. `--policy` takes a Rego file, the name of a shipped policy (`pure-only`, `provenance-only`) or a JSON file. Exit 1 when the policy denies, 2 when it cannot be parsed or evaluated. A holo that carries signed provenance and proof statements reaches P1 and P2 only when `--key`, or a certificate identity and issuer, names the signer that signed them.

verbs.name: images
verbs.summary: The `images` module's verbs. `build`, `inspect`, `pull`, `push` and `verify` are each the same command as the flat verb it names (`verify` is `check`). `ls`, `tag`, `rm` and `prune` read and change the local image store (`$PRISM_IMAGES`, else `$PRISM_HOME/images`): `ls` lists repository, tag, image id, created and size; `rm` untags one of several tags and removes an image only when no container references it, unless `--force`; `prune` removes untagged images no container references, and with `--all` every image none references. `images` alone is `images ls`, and the top-level verbs `tag` and `rmi` are `images tag` and `images rm`. `prism-code images --help` lists them.

verbs.name: containers
verbs.summary: The `containers` module's verbs: `create`, `inspect`, `logs`, `ls`, `ps`, `rm`, `run` and `start`. `run`, `rm` and `inspect` are the flat verbs they name; `create` prints the new container's id, `ps` lists running containers (every one with `--all`), `ls` is `ps`, and `logs` prints a container's stored output. The top-level verbs `ps` and `logs` are `containers ps` and `containers logs`, and the singular spellings `container`, `image` and `volume` name the same groups as `containers`, `images` and `volumes`. `prism-code containers --help` lists them.

verbs.name: volumes
verbs.summary: The `volumes` module's verbs: `create`, `inspect`, `ls` and `rm`, over the capability grant and provider declarations of a project's prism.toml. A volume is a declared store, never a host folder; `create` prints the names of the variables a provider returned, never their values. `prism-code volumes --help` lists them.

verbs.name: push
verbs.summary: Put the holo in an OCI registry or a local store as a deterministic manifest, each attestation a referrer. With `--key` or `--keyless`, also sign a statement naming the manifest, so `cosign verify-attestation` passes on the same reference. With no holo, push the image of that name in the local image store.

verbs.name: pull
verbs.summary: Fetch a holo and write it only after its digests, archive, verdict and attestations pass; the signer flags are those of `verify-attestation`. A reference is `registry/repo:tag`, `@sha256:`, `@blake3:` or `dir://`. A verified holo is also kept in the local image store under the name it was pulled by.

verbs.name: dev
verbs.summary: Watch the project, rebuild and re-check on every change, and serve the local studio at `http://localhost:4100`, with a Check tab and a Replay tab. The page loads nothing from outside the machine.

verbs.name: skill
verbs.summary: With `--out`, copy the `prism` skill this package ships, `SKILL.md` and its references, into that folder; it reads only the package and never writes to a default place. `init` writes the same files into the project. With `verify`, judge a copy again. The skill gate is a LexLean model (`skills/gate`) whose eleven theorems Lean's kernel proves here, now, in about two seconds: a skill passes only when its `SKILL.md` has the BLAKE3 label prism-code pins, the gate model is the pinned one, every `prism-code` command it names ships in this CLI, it names no server tool, it links no host outside Prism's own sites, holds nothing shaped like a credential and no executable file, nothing would send a model, and every theorem the gate declares is proved. Every fact is computed from the bytes and the code, never declared by the skill.

verbs.name: build
verbs.summary: Check the project as `check` does, then write the app under `.prism/build` with nothing compiled, and replay its acceptance vectors. A rule app is written as the verified rule judge with the model's numbers; any other text application as a holo whose guest is one pinned evaluator running the model's program, refused unless that guest answers the model's own examples as its definitions do. `--out` also copies what was built into that folder, and `--check` stops after the check. `--json` prints one `prism/report/1` report. Every step runs in this process: no server, no container and nothing sent.

verbs.name: verify
verbs.summary: With a holo: verify its digests and its world within the grant, and replay every acceptance vector on a fresh instance. With a project, or nothing: check the model and prove every theorem again, require what is built to be the build of the model as it is on disk, then do the same for it. The assurance level is reported, and judged only when `--policy` names a policy. `--json` prints one `prism/report/1` report. Exit 0 when it passed, 1 when a theorem is not proved, a vector fails, nothing is built or the build is stale, 2 when the manifest or the model does not check.

verbs.name: system
verbs.summary: Report on this installation and tidy it, with the verbs info, version, events, df and prune: `info` and `version` name the package, the holo format, the runtime and the toolchain and builder image the project's `prismpm.lock` pins; `events` prints container create, start, die and destroy events from the container store and follows it until `--until`; `df` says what the container records and the local image store take; `prune` removes exited containers, then untagged images no container references (with `--all`, every such image), asking first unless `--force`.

verbs.name: auth
verbs.summary: Log in to a registry or out of it, with the verbs login and logout. `login` checks the username and password with the registry, then stores them with the registry logins on this machine, so `push` and `pull` find them; the password comes from `--password-stdin` or a prompt that does not echo, never from the command line. `logout` removes the credential from every store that holds it.

verbs.name: login
verbs.summary: The same as `prism-code auth login`.

verbs.name: logout
verbs.summary: The same as `prism-code auth logout`.

verbs.name: ps
verbs.summary: The same as `prism-code containers ps`.

verbs.name: logs
verbs.summary: The same as `prism-code containers logs`.

verbs.name: tag
verbs.summary: The same as `prism-code images tag`.

verbs.name: rmi
verbs.summary: The same as `prism-code images rm`.

providers.$comment: Provider services (#294, experimental). The wire protocol is on the manifest reference page.
providers.discovery: An executable named `prism-provider-<type>` on the PATH is found the way a plugin is, and is not a plugin: `prism-code provider-<type>` is not a command, and the `provider-` prefix is reserved.

firstParty.name: kv
firstParty.usage: provider = { type = "kv", options = { store, dir, set } }
firstParty.summary: A local key-value store, kept as one JSON file under `.prism/kv`. Returns `URL` and `STORE`. `up` never overwrites a key, and `down` deletes the file. Ships in the prism-code package.

plugins.$comment: CLI plugins (#293, experimental). `--help` prints them under a Plugins heading, apart from the verbs above.
plugins.discovery: An executable named `prism-<name>` on the PATH runs as `prism-code <name>`, and `prism <name>` once the CLI is renamed. On Windows the first `PATHEXT` extension found in a directory wins and names are case-insensitive. The first PATH directory that has the plugin wins, and a built-in verb always wins over a plugin.
plugins.contract: A plugin answers `prism-<name> prism-cli-plugin-metadata` with JSON: `schemaVersion` "1", `vendor`, `version`, `shortDescription` and optional `errorHooks`, a list of verbs. A plugin that does not answer is listed as invalid and never runs. Arguments reach the plugin unchanged and its exit code is the command's.
plugins.hooks: When a verb a plugin names in `errorHooks` exits non-zero, prism-code runs `prism-<name> prism-cli-plugin-hooks` with `{"schemaVersion":"1","command","args","exitCode"}` on stdin and prints the `messages` it returns under What's next, at most ten lines. Set `PRISM_CODE_NO_HOOKS=1` to turn hooks off.

firstParty.name: doctor
firstParty.summary: Check Node.js and the optional sigstore packages; exit 1 when a check fails. Ships in the prism-code package. prism-code needs nothing else: check, build and verify run in this process.

verbs.name: init
verbs.summary: Scaffold a new application: `prism.toml`, `examples/`, `intent.md`, a default capability set and the lockfile.

flags.meaning: Which type source the scaffold writes.
Starting examples and intent.
Overwrite files that already exist.

verbs.name: build
verbs.summary: Compile the model into a holo inside the pinned SDK image, record provenance and the proof attestation, and cache the result by spec digest.

flags.meaning: How much the provenance records. `max` adds every resolved input and the full toolchain environment.
Skip provenance. Unsafe: the holo cannot pass `check` above P0.
Rebuild even when the spec digest is unchanged.
Apply the matching overlay, `prism.browser.toml` or `prism.node.toml`.

verbs.name: check
verbs.summary: Verify the holo's digest, provenance, proof, lockfile pins and declared world against a policy, then print a verdict with the assurance level and reasons.

flags.meaning: Policy to judge against.
Do not contact the transparency log or any registry. Missing data exits 2.

verbs.name: run
verbs.summary: Instantiate the holo after `check` passes at the policy's level, then grant exactly the capability set it declares.

flags.meaning: One input to dispatch. Omit it to read inputs line by line.
Policy the gate judges against.
Run even when `check` fails. Prints a warning on every start.
Remove the container when it exits. One input only.
Serve the instance over HTTP instead of dispatching once.

verbs.name: dev
verbs.summary: Watch the model, rebuild and re-check on every change, and serve a local studio with Check and Replay tabs.

flags.meaning: Studio port.
Do not open the studio in a browser.
Policy the Check tab judges against.
The build to run, in a shell.
The file the build writes.

verbs.name: replay
verbs.summary: Re-execute recorded histories against a build and fail on any divergence, reporting every one.

flags.meaning: Which image to replay against.
Write the `prism/replay/v1` statement there, also when the replay diverged.

verbs.name: push
verbs.summary: Push a holo and its attestations to an OCI registry. The attestations travel as referrers of the holo.

flags.meaning: Push to a local directory store instead of a registry.
Push the holo only. The pushed holo checks at P0.

verbs.name: pull
verbs.summary: Pull a holo and its attestations from an OCI registry or a local directory store.

flags.meaning: Pull from a local directory store.
Run `check` on the pulled holo and exit with its code.

verbs.name: deploy
verbs.summary: Publish the holo to a GitHub repository and GitHub Pages, serving its attestations alongside it.

flags.meaning: Repository to publish to.
Branch GitHub Pages serves.
Push the repository only.

verbs.name: export
verbs.summary: Write the six-file browser export, a tarball, or a runnable OCI image that `docker run` serves.

flags.meaning: Where the browser export is written.
Write one tarball instead of a directory.
Write a runnable OCI image under this name.

verbs.name: inspect
verbs.summary: Print the manifest, section digests, format revision, world and attestations of a holo without running it.

flags.meaning: Print one part only.
Print the security view: signers, trusted base, capability set, theorem list.
With `--audit`, write the report to a file.

verbs.name: attest
verbs.summary: Add a signed statement to a holo. Signing is keyless by default.

flags.meaning: JSON file holding the predicate.
Predicate type URI.
Sign with a local key for air-gapped use instead of keyless.

verbs.name: verify
verbs.summary: Check a signed statement on a holo against the signing identity you expect.

flags.meaning: Identity the statement must be signed by.
Issuer that identity must come from.
Verify statements of one predicate type only.
Verify against a local public key instead of keyless.

verbs.name: generate
verbs.summary: Regenerate the JS, Rust and Python bindings and the typed client from the world. Nothing is written when nothing changed.

flags.meaning: Output path. There is no default, so nothing lands in `node_modules` or another place you did not name.
Which bindings to write.

verbs.name: lock
verbs.summary: Write or refresh the lockfile from the current model and inputs, without building. Pins that still resolve stay as they are, and the SDK image and toolchain pins do not move. Exits 2 when there is no lockfile or its SDK cannot be resolved.

flags.meaning: Write nothing. Fail when the lockfile is stale and name the pins that differ.

verbs.name: update
verbs.summary: Move the lockfile forward and print the old and new digests of every pin that changed. Without a flag it refreshes the toolchain pins; with `--toolchain` it also pins a new SDK image. Exits 2 when the lockfile or the image cannot be resolved.

flags.meaning: SDK image to pin, as `name@sha256:digest`.
Standards lock the new image selects. Needs `--toolchain`.
Print the change without writing the lockfile.
